addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

`all_hanta/ncbi_dataset/data/protein.faa` has **16,950** `>` header lines, but many of them are the same protein accession repeated back-to-back (e.g. `AIR07773.1` appears 13 times, and there are many others like it — 1,446 duplicate occurrences total across the file). This happens because NCBI's Datasets download bundles one protein FASTA entry per CDS annotation, and the same protein accession can be annotated on multiple genome/assembly records.

The pipeline's `parse_fasta()` (`all_hanta.py:800`) builds a dict keyed by accession with `index.setdefault(acc, record)` — so repeat occurrences of an already-seen accession are silently dropped, keeping only the first. The logged count comes from `indexed_record_count()` (`all_hanta.py:717`), which counts distinct record objects, i.e. de-duplicated accessions:

```
16,950 raw FASTA entries − 1,446 duplicate occurrences = 15,504  ✓ matches the log exactly
```

So **15,504 is the correct count of unique protein accessions in your locally downloaded package** — nothing was lost by a bug, the raw file just has redundant entries.

**Why 15,568 on the NCBI Virus website differs from 15,504 locally:**
That's a separate, smaller gap (64 sequences) between your downloaded package and the live NCBI Virus count — not something your pipeline is doing. The most likely explanations are:
- **Timing** — NCBI Virus reflects the database at query time; your `all_hanta.zip`/package is a snapshot from whenever it was downloaded, and new Orthohantavirus proteins get added/suppressed regularly.
- **Different query scope** — NCBI Virus's "Orthohantavirus" protein count may use a slightly different filter (e.g., including/excluding certain unverified or third-party-annotated sequences) than the NCBI Datasets `datasets download virus genome taxon` package you have.

There's no date/version stamp in this package's README or `dataset_catalog.json` to pin down exactly when it was pulled — if you want to close that 64-sequence gap precisely, re-downloading the dataset package fresh from NCBI Datasets and re-running the pipeline would sync it back up with whatever NCBI Virus shows today.

content.text:
Not necessary — leave it as is. Reasoning:

- The 15,504 vs 16,950 gap is fully explained (duplicate accessions, correctly deduplicated) — that's not staleness, it's correct behavior.
- The remaining 15,504 vs 15,568 gap is ~0.4% and is just the normal drift between any downloaded snapshot and a live, continuously-updated database. NCBI Virus will basically never match a static package exactly — new sequences get submitted daily.
- Re-downloading now just resets the clock; by tomorrow you'd have a new (probably still nonzero) gap. Chasing it isn't productive unless currency is itself the requirement.

When it *would* be worth re-pulling:
- You're doing time-sensitive surveillance (e.g., tracking a new outbreak/strain) where the newest few sequences matter.
- You're about to publish/report final numbers and want the freshest possible snapshot as of that date.

Otherwise, a fixed snapshot is actually preferable — it makes your pipeline's output reproducible and stable rather than shifting every time you rerun it. I'd say keep the current `all_hanta.zip` as your working dataset unless you have a specific reason to refresh.

1	# Orthohantavirus NCBI Dataset Preparation Pipeline
2	
3	`all_hanta.py` — version 2.0.0
4	
5	A reproducible pipeline that ingests an NCBI Datasets **Orthohantavirus** package and produces
6	accession-, isolate-, species- and host-level tables, pathogenicity labels, per-segment divergence
7	diagnostics, and ML-ready feature matrices for host-association and risk-classification work.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Step 0 — Download the data
12	
13	```bash
14	datasets download virus genome taxon 1980442 \
15	  --include genome,cds,protein,annotation,biosample \
16	  --filename all_hanta.zip
17	
18	unzip all_hanta.zip -d all_hanta
19	```
20	
21	## Step 1 — Stop git from corrupting the package
22	
23	**Do this before anything else.** The package ships an `md5sum.txt` containing checksums of the
24	exact bytes NCBI published. On Windows, `git config core.autocrlf=true` rewrites LF to CRLF on
25	checkout for anything git considers text, which changes those bytes, breaks every checksum, and
26	makes results differ between Linux and Windows checkouts.
27	
28	The repo's `.gitattributes` marks the package binary to prevent this. If your working copy was
29	already mangled, repair it once:
30	
31	```bash
32	rm -f all_hanta/ncbi_dataset/data/* all_hanta/md5sum.txt all_hanta/README.md
33	git checkout -- all_hanta/
34	```
35	
36	The pipeline verifies before doing any work, so you will know immediately either way.
37	
38	## Step 2 — Run
39	
40	```bash
41	python all_hanta.py --input . --output output
42	```
43	
44	| Argument | Default | Purpose |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `--input` | `.` | Package root containing `all_hanta/ncbi_dataset/data` |
47	| `--output` | `<input>/output` | Output directory |
48	| `--allow-checksum-mismatch` | off | Proceed despite failed integrity check (mismatch still recorded) |
49	| `--cluster-threshold` | `0.02` | Cosine k-mer distance for within-species single-linkage clustering |
50	| `--max-features` | `200` | Number of top-variance k-mer features in the ML matrix |
51	| `--min-species-size` | `8` | Minimum assessable isolates before divergence diagnostics are computed |
52	| `--verbose` | off | Debug logging |
53	
54	The transform is GIL-bound and runs serially; a full run takes ~16s on the 15,991-record package.
55	
56	Requires Python 3.11+ (uses `datetime.UTC`) with `pandas`, `pyarrow`, `numpy`. No alignment or
57	phylogenetics dependencies.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## Reproducibility model
62	
63	Integrity is established against NCBI's own published checksums, never against digests this
64	script invents.
65	
66	**File level.** `md5sum.txt` is parsed and every shipped file verified. On mismatch the pipeline
67	also tests the CRLF-normalized form purely to *diagnose* the cause, then aborts:
68	
69	```
70	CHECKSUM MISMATCH data_report.jsonl
71	    expected (NCBI): 9c228361ec1892882d118876fcdd263e
72	    observed (disk): 24dcee9c3c910a59c67093ab818135e7
73	    diagnosis      : on-disk bytes are CRLF but NCBI published the LF form ...
74	```
75	
76	**Content level.** `nucleotide.sequenceHash` (CRC32, emitted per record by NCBI) is used for
77	sequence identity and de-duplication. It is independent of line endings and platform, so it
78	behaves identically everywhere even on a mangled checkout. NCBI strips leading zeros from these
79	values — observed widths in this package are 5–8 characters — so they are **zero-padded to 8**
80	before any comparison. They also expose 3,393 exact resubmissions (12,598 distinct hashes over
81	15,991 records) that would otherwise inflate group sizes.
82	
83	`hashlib` is still used, but only to hash the pipeline's own outputs and configuration.
84	
85	Runs are deterministic: two consecutive runs produce byte-identical table contents, and
86	`ortho_summary.json` contains no absolute paths.
87	
88	---
89	
90	## Taxonomy resolution
91	
92	The organism-level `virus.taxId` is **not** usable as a species key. In this package it takes
93	**553 distinct values**, mixing strain-level taxa (`Hantaan virus Lee` 11601, `Four Corners
94	hantavirus` 31621) with legacy/current taxid pairs for the same species (`Puumala orthohantavirus`
95	1980486 vs `Orthohantavirus puumalaense` 3052493).
96	
97	The node immediately below genus *Orthohantavirus* (taxId 1980442) in `virus.lineage` **is** the
98	ICTV species. Canonicalising on its binomial name merges the legacy/current pairs, collapsing
99	553 organism values to **38 species** plus `unclassified Orthohantavirus` (2,339 records).
100	
101	The remaining `virus.lineage` nodes supply every higher rank for free, giving the full grouping
102	hierarchy that terminates naturally at the top:
103	
104	```
105	accession → isolate → species → subfamily Mammantavirinae → family Hantaviridae
106	          → order Elliovirales → class Bunyaviricetes → phylum Negarnaviricota
107	```
108	
109	Records that are unclassified or genus-only are retained with `species_status` set accordingly —
110	never silently merged into a named species.
111	
112	## Isolate grouping
113	
114	BioSample is present on only **87 of 15,991** records (0.54%), so a BioSample-first cascade
115	almost never fires. `isolate.name` is present on 15,491 records (96.9%) and is the field
116	submitters actually use to tie an isolate's S, M and L segments together.
117	
118	| Tier | Key | Confidence |
119	|---|---|---|
120	| 1 | species + biosample + isolate | 1.00 |
121	| 2 | species + `isolate.name` | 0.95 |
122	| 3 | species + normalized isolate/strain label | 0.90 |
123	| 4 | species + strain + collection date + location | 0.75 |
124	| 5 | species + strain + location | 0.65 |
125	| — | accession only | 0.10 |
126	
127	Result on this package: **1,777 groups with all three S, M and L segments present**, and 222
128	where all three are coding-complete. The coding-complete count is bounded by the data — only
129	1,339 of 15,991 records are `COMPLETE` at all — not by the grouping.
130	
131	## Segment resolution
132	
133	The `segment` field is dirtier than a three-value check assumes. Values observed here include
134	`Partial L`, `S segment`, `M-segment`, `M; medium`, `small (S)`, `G1`, `G2`, `ANONYMOUS`, `s`
135	and `N`, plus 3,558 records with no `segment` field at all. Evidence is applied in order:
136	
137	| `segment_source` | Basis | Confidence | Count |
138	|---|---|---|---|
139	| `explicit` | normalized `segment` field (`G1`/`G2` → M, `N` → S) | 1.00 | 12,431 |
140	| `annotation` | CDS product-name majority vote | 0.90 | 3,117 |
141	| `defline` | genomic FASTA description | 0.75 | 104 |
142	| `length_heuristic` | falls in exactly one ICTV size band | 0.40 | 129 |
143	| `unresolved` | — | 0.00 | 210 |
144	
145	Unresolved segments drop from 405 to 210.
146	
147	## Completeness
148	
149	NCBI's structured `completeness` is present on 100% of records and is authoritative
150	(PARTIAL 14,652 / COMPLETE 1,339). Length is used only to qualify a COMPLETE call as
151	coding-complete, never to override NCBI. ICTV segment sizes: S 1.2–2.1 kb, M 3.4–3.8 kb,
152	L 6.5–6.6 kb. The pipeline applies S and M as stated and widens L to 6.3–6.8 kb, because
153	submitted L segments sit just outside the ICTV figure at both ends; see the note on
154	`SEGMENT_LENGTH_RANGE` in `all_hanta.py`.
155	
156	Length anomalies are flagged only where they contradict those ranges: partial sequences are
157	*expected* to be short. This drops length warnings from 5,856 to 9.
158	
159	## Host classification
160	
161	Host role is derived from `host.lineage` rank, not substring matching:
162	
163	| Observed | Count | Role |
164	|---|---|---|
165	| Rodentia | 11,043 | `reservoir_rodent` |
166	| *Homo sapiens* | 2,091 | `spillover_host_human` |
167	| Eulipotyphla | 1,035 | `reservoir_shrew_mole` |
168	| Chiroptera | 83 | `reservoir_bat` |
169	| `isLabHost` true | 338 | `laboratory_host` |
170	
171	`isLabHost`, `labHost` and `isVaccineStrain` are authoritative NCBI fields and are used directly;
172	lab-derived and vaccine records are excluded from the ML matrix.
173	
174	**Host jumps.** Each record's host order is compared against its species' expected reservoir
175	order. 33 records are pathogenic viruses recovered outside their reservoir order — SEOV in
176	Chinese shrews and bats, ANDV-clade sequences in Brazilian bats. These are documented
177	host-sharing observations, not data errors, and are surfaced as
178	`host_jump_status = host_order_mismatch` and weighted in the risk score.
179	
180	## Pathogenicity labels
181	
182	`SPECIES_RISK` covers 38 species. Every entry carries its source URL. Species **absent** from the
183	table are labelled `unknown` — never silently "non-pathogenic".
184	
185	CFR estimates genuinely conflict between sources, so the reported range is stored verbatim
186	alongside an ordinal band for modelling. Do not collapse them to a point estimate.
187	
188	| Class | Species | CFR band |
189	|---|---|---|
190	| `pathogenic_hcps` | ANDV, SNV, CHOV, LANV, RIOMV, BAYV, BCCV | up to `high_gt_30pct` |
191	| `pathogenic_hfrs` | HTNV, DOBV, SEOV, PUUV | `low_lt_1pct` – `moderate_1_15pct` |
192	| `rare_or_opportunistic` | TULV | `low_lt_1pct` |
193	| `suspected` | THAIV, SANGV | `unknown` |
194	| `no_known_human_disease` | shrew-, mole- and bat-borne species | `none_known` |
195	| `unknown` | anything not curated | `unknown` |
196	
197	HTNV is reported as both ~1% and 5–15% depending on source; both appear in `cfr_reported_range`.
198	ANDV is the only orthohantavirus with documented person-to-person transmission. TULV is held out
199	of `pathogenic_hfrs` deliberately — lumping its handful of mild case reports with HTNV/DOBV would
200	put 2,123 records into the same class as the viruses that actually drive HFRS mortality.
201	
202	**Curation audit.** Curated reservoirs are checked against the modal observed host order on every
203	run. Six of the original 38 entries disagreed with the package's own host annotations at the order
204	level (asikkalaense, fugongense, lankaense, luxiense, sagercreekense, tigrayense) and were
205	corrected against the data. The audit runs every invocation so this class of error cannot silently
206	return.
207	
208	## Reassortment — not called, and why
209	
210	**This pipeline does not call reassortment.** A classifier that did was built and then withdrawn
211	after it failed validation against the literature.
212	
213	The literature reports reassortment as frequent in PUUV (19.1–32% in Finnish studies), SNV, DOBV
214	and TULV, and absent or sparse in ANDV. Measured on this dataset, the classifier produced the
215	inverse ranking:
216	
217	| Species | n | flagged | literature |
218	|---|---|---|---|
219	| ANDV | 68 | 72.1% | absent or sparse |
220	| CHOV | 8 | 100.0% | not reported |
221	| DOBV | 62 | 38.7% | frequent |
222	| PUUV | 416 | 7.7% | frequent (19.1–32%) |
223	| TULV | 313 | 3.5% | frequent |
224	
225	Sweeping the discordance threshold from 0.25 to 0.85 scaled all rates down without ever changing
226	the ordering. The cause is intrinsic to the metric: cosine distance on 3-mer amino-acid
227	composition tracks within-species sequence diversity and sample size, not tree topology. Species
228	represented by many near-identical outbreak sequences get stable neighbour orderings and few
229	flags; species represented by a handful of divergent, scattered sequences get noisy orderings and
230	many flags. CHOV at 100% with n=8 is the clearest symptom.
231	
232	What is emitted instead, in `ortho_segment_divergence.parquet`, is the honest underlying
233	measurement — per-segment nearest neighbours, k-mer distances, and normalized rank separations
234	(`sl_rank_separation`, `m_rank_offset`) — with every assessable isolate marked
235	`requires_phylogenetic_confirmation`.
236	
237	**To detect reassortment properly**, build per-segment alignments (MAFFT) and trees (IQ-TREE) and
238	test topological incongruence between the S, M and L trees. The constraints worth testing against:
239	M-segment exchange dominates, S and L cosegregate from the same parent, and events occur within a
240	reservoir host species or between sympatric lineages.
241	
242	The one trustworthy reassortment-adjacent signal here is `taxonomic_incongruence`: one isolate
243	label whose segments NCBI assigned to more than one species (70 isolates). That is metadata, not
244	inference, and it does feed the risk score. It is computed across groups, not within — the
245	grouping key contains the species, so a within-group check can never fire.
246	
247	## Species clustering
248	
249	Within-species single-linkage clustering on cosine distance over 3-mer profiles of the
250	concatenated N+GPC proteins. Columns are named `kmer_cluster_id` and `kmer_distance_threshold`,
251	deliberately **not** `ped_*`.
252	
253	The ICTV species criterion for Hantaviridae is DEmARC with a pairwise evolutionary distance cutoff
254	of **0.1** under the WAG substitution model, which requires multiple sequence alignment and
255	maximum-likelihood inference. These clusters are an alignment-free proxy and are not PED values.
256	`ortho_summary.json` restates this.
257	
258	---
259	
260	## Outputs
261	
262	| File | Rows × Cols | Contents |
263	|---|---|---|
264	| `ortho_accession_table.parquet` | 15,991 × 55 | One row per accession: taxonomy ranks, segment, completeness, host, pathogenicity, host-jump status, QC flags |
265	| `ortho_species_table.parquet` | 39 × 32 | One row per canonical ICTV species: merged taxids, legacy synonyms, risk profile, segment and host counts |
266	| `ortho_isolate_table.parquet` | 9,904 × 52 | Reconstructed isolates with S/M/L representatives, triplet status, concatenated protein, divergence diagnostics |
267	| `ortho_host_table.parquet` | 253 × 13 | One row per host taxon with risk prior and virus species carried |
268	| `ortho_risk_table.parquet` | 9,904 × 31 | Pathogenicity class, CFR band, citation, and an auditable additive `surveillance_priority_score` |
269	| `ortho_segment_divergence.parquet` | 9,904 × 17 | Per-segment nearest neighbours and rank separations — **diagnostics, not reassortment calls** |
270	| `ortho_ml_feature_matrix.parquet` | 7,529 × 228 | Raw features + labels, with `group_id` and `year` for leakage-free CV |
271	| `ortho_ml_segments.parquet` | 15,781 × 19 | Segment-level table for per-segment models |
272	| `ortho_suppressed.parquet` | 1,021 × 16 | Non-representative accessions with the reason |
273	| `ortho_qc_report.parquet` | 15,991 × 11 | Per-accession QC including failed transforms with traceback |
274	| `ortho_feature_scaling.json` | — | Per-feature mean/std, to be fitted **inside** your CV fold |
275	| `ortho_summary.json` | — | Provenance, integrity results, counts, methods and stated limitations |
276	
277	### Risk score
278	
279	`surveillance_priority_score` is a transparent sum, with every term emitted as its own column so
280	it can be audited or re-weighted:
281	
282	| Term | Weight |
283	|---|---|
284	| `priority_cfr_term` | 4.0 / 2.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.0 by CFR band |
285	| `priority_human_spillover_term` | 2.0 if human-derived |
286	| `priority_taxonomic_incongruence_term` | 1.5 |
287	| `priority_host_jump_term` | 1.0 |
288	| `priority_triplet_term` | 1.0 if coding-complete triplet |
289	| `priority_nss_term` | 0.5 if an NSs ORF is annotated |
290	
291	This is a triage aid for surveillance, not a validated epidemiological risk model. No term derives
292	from the k-mer divergence diagnostics — weighting a withdrawn classifier would have propagated an
293	artefact of sample size into a ranking meant to guide surveillance.
294	
295	### Using the ML tables
296	
297	Features are emitted **raw**. Fit scaling inside your cross-validation fold using
298	`ortho_feature_scaling.json`; the statistics there were computed on the full table and must not be
299	applied before splitting. Feature selection is unsupervised (top-variance k-mers).
300	
301	**Split by `group_id` (species) or by `year`.** A random split badly overstates accuracy on this
302	data, because segments from the same outbreak are near-identical.
303	
304	---
305	
306	## Known limitations
307	
308	- **No reassortment calls.** See above. Requires MAFFT + IQ-TREE.
309	- **k-mer distances are not PED.** The ICTV 0.1 cutoff needs aligned sequences and ML inference.
310	- **222 coding-complete triplets** is a ceiling set by the data (1,339 COMPLETE records total),
311	  not by the pipeline. 1,777 groups have all three segments present at some completeness.
312	- **2,386 records are `unclassified Orthohantavirus` or genus-only** and carry no species-level
313	  risk label. They are retained, not discarded.
314	- **CFR bands are literature ranges, not computed from this data.** Sources conflict; both values
315	  are recorded where they do.
316	- **1,719 records have no host** and 3,703 have no collection date.
317	- Grouping tiers 4 and 5 rarely fire, because `strain` is only populated from BioSample.
318	- Only the first BioSample accession in a record is resolved.
319	
320	## Citations
321	
322	- ICTV *Hantaviridae* / *Orthohantavirus* — species demarcation, segment sizes:
323	  <https://ictv.global/report/chapter/hantaviridae/hantaviridae/mammantavirinae/orthohantavirus>
324	- Zoonotic Hantaviridae with global public health significance — pathogenicity, CFR, reservoirs:
325	  <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10459939/>
326	- Reassortment events in the evolution of hantaviruses — frequencies, segment constraints:
327	  <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6153690/>
328	- ECDC factsheet on orthohantavirus infections:
329	  <https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/infectious-disease-topics/hantavirus-infection/factsheet-orthohantavirus-infections>
330	- NCBI Datasets virus data report schema:
331	  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/docs/v2/reference-docs/data-reports/virus/>
332


Records that are unclassified or genus-only are retained with `species_status` set accordingly —
never silently merged into a named species.

## Isolate grouping

BioSample is present on only **87 of 15,991** records (0.54%), so a BioSample-first cascade
almost never fires. `isolate.name` is present on 15,491 records (96.9%) and is the field
submitters actually use to tie an isolate's S, M and L segments together.

| Tier | Key | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | species + biosample + isolate | 1.00 |
| 2 | species + `isolate.name` | 0.95 |
| 3 | species + normalized isolate/strain label | 0.90 |
| 4 | species + strain + collection date + location | 0.75 |
| 5 | species + strain + location | 0.65 |
| — | accession only | 0.10 |

Result on this package: **1,777 groups with all three S, M and L segments present**, and 222
where all three are coding-complete. The coding-complete count is bounded by the data — only
1,339 of 15,991 records are `COMPLETE` at all — not by the grouping.

## Segment resolution

The `segment` field is dirtier than a three-value check assumes. Values observed here include
`Partial L`, `S segment`, `M-segment`, `M; medium`, `small (S)`, `G1`, `G2`, `ANONYMOUS`, `s`
and `N`, plus 3,558 records with no `segment` field at all. Evidence is applied in order:

| `segment_source` | Basis | Confidence | Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| `explicit` | normalized `segment` field (`G1`/`G2` → M, `N` → S) | 1.00 | 12,431 |
| `annotation` | CDS product-name majority vote | 0.90 | 3,117 |
| `defline` | genomic FASTA description | 0.75 | 104 |
| `length_heuristic` | falls in exactly one ICTV size band | 0.40 | 129 |
| `unresolved` | — | 0.00 | 210 |

Unresolved segments drop from 405 to 210.

## Completeness

NCBI's structured `completeness` is present on 100% of records and is authoritative
(PARTIAL 14,652 / COMPLETE 1,339). Length is used only to qualify a COMPLETE call as
coding-complete, never to override NCBI. ICTV segment sizes: S 1.2–2.1 kb, M 3.4–3.8 kb,
L 6.5–6.6 kb. The pipeline applies S and M as stated and widens L to 6.3–6.8 kb, because
submitted L segments sit just outside the ICTV figure at both ends; see the note on
`SEGMENT_LENGTH_RANGE` in `all_hanta.py`.

Length anomalies are flagged only where they contradict those ranges: partial sequences are
*expected* to be short. This drops length warnings from 5,856 to 9.

## Host classification

Host role is derived from `host.lineage` rank, not substring matching:

| Observed | Count | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Rodentia | 11,043 | `reservoir_rodent` |
| *Homo sapiens* | 2,091 | `spillover_host_human` |
| Eulipotyphla | 1,035 | `reservoir_shrew_mole` |
| Chiroptera | 83 | `reservoir_bat` |
| `isLabHost` true | 338 | `laboratory_host` |

`isLabHost`, `labHost` and `isVaccineStrain` are authoritative NCBI fields and are used directly;
lab-derived and vaccine records are excluded from the ML matrix.

**Host jumps.** Each record's host order is compared against its species' expected reservoir
order. 33 records are pathogenic viruses recovered outside their reservoir order — SEOV in
Chinese shrews and bats, ANDV-clade sequences in Brazilian bats. These are documented
host-sharing observations, not data errors, and are surfaced as
`host_jump_status = host_order_mismatch` and weighted in the risk score.

## Pathogenicity labels

`SPECIES_RISK` covers 38 species. Every entry carries its source URL. Species **absent** from the
table are labelled `unknown` — never silently "non-pathogenic".

CFR estimates genuinely conflict between sources, so the reported range is stored verbatim
alongside an ordinal band for modelling. Do not collapse them to a point estimate.

| Class | Species | CFR band |
|---|---|---|
| `pathogenic_hcps` | ANDV, SNV, CHOV, LANV, RIOMV, BAYV, BCCV | up to `high_gt_30pct` |
| `pathogenic_hfrs` | HTNV, DOBV, SEOV, PUUV | `low_lt_1pct` – `moderate_1_15pct` |
| `rare_or_opportunistic` | TULV | `low_lt_1pct` |
| `suspected` | THAIV, SANGV | `unknown` |
| `no_known_human_disease` | shrew-, mole- and bat-borne species | `none_known` |
| `unknown` | anything not curated | `unknown` |

HTNV is reported as both ~1% and 5–15% depending on source; both appear in `cfr_reported_range`.
ANDV is the only orthohantavirus with documented person-to-person transmission. TULV is held out
of `pathogenic_hfrs` deliberately — lumping its handful of mild case reports with HTNV/DOBV would
put 2,123 records into the same class as the viruses that actually drive HFRS mortality.

**Curation audit.** Curated reservoirs are checked against the modal observed host order on every
run. Six of the original 38 entries disagreed with the package's own host annotations at the order
level (asikkalaense, fugongense, lankaense, luxiense, sagercreekense, tigrayense) and were
corrected against the data. The audit runs every invocation so this class of error cannot silently
return.

## Reassortment — not called, and why

**This pipeline does not call reassortment.** A classifier that did was built and then withdrawn
after it failed validation against the literature.

The literature reports reassortment as frequent in PUUV (19.1–32% in Finnish studies), SNV, DOBV
and TULV, and absent or sparse in ANDV. Measured on this dataset, the classifier produced the
inverse ranking:

| Species | n | flagged | literature |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANDV | 68 | 72.1% | absent or sparse |
| CHOV | 8 | 100.0% | not reported |
| DOBV | 62 | 38.7% | frequent |
| PUUV | 416 | 7.7% | frequent (19.1–32%) |
| TULV | 313 | 3.5% | frequent |

Sweeping the discordance threshold from 0.25 to 0.85 scaled all rates down without ever changing
the ordering. The cause is intrinsic to the metric: cosine distance on 3-mer amino-acid
composition tracks within-species sequence diversity and sample size, not tree topology. Species
represented by many near-identical outbreak sequences get stable neighbour orderings and few
flags; species represented by a handful of divergent, scattered sequences get noisy orderings and
many flags. CHOV at 100% with n=8 is the clearest symptom.

What is emitted instead, in `ortho_segment_divergence.parquet`, is the honest underlying
measurement — per-segment nearest neighbours, k-mer distances, and normalized rank separations
(`sl_rank_separation`, `m_rank_offset`) — with every assessable isolate marked
`requires_phylogenetic_confirmation`.

**To detect reassortment properly**, build per-segment alignments (MAFFT) and trees (IQ-TREE) and
test topological incongruence between the S, M and L trees. The constraints worth testing against:
M-segment exchange dominates, S and L cosegregate from the same parent, and events occur within a
reservoir host species or between sympatric lineages.

The one trustworthy reassortment-adjacent signal here is `taxonomic_incongruence`: one isolate
label whose segments NCBI assigned to more than one species (70 isolates). That is metadata, not
inference, and it does feed the risk score. It is computed across groups, not within — the
grouping key contains the species, so a within-group check can never fire.

## Species clustering

Within-species single-linkage clustering on cosine distance over 3-mer profiles of the
concatenated N+GPC proteins. Columns are named `kmer_cluster_id` and `kmer_distance_threshold`,
deliberately **not** `ped_*`.

The ICTV species criterion for Hantaviridae is DEmARC with a pairwise evolutionary distance cutoff
of **0.1** under the WAG substitution model, which requires multiple sequence alignment and
maximum-likelihood inference. These clusters are an alignment-free proxy and are not PED values.
`ortho_summary.json` restates this.

---

## Outputs

| File | Rows × Cols | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `ortho_accession_table.parquet` | 15,991 × 55 | One row per accession: taxonomy ranks, segment, completeness, host, pathogenicity, host-jump status, QC flags |
| `ortho_species_table.parquet` | 39 × 32 | One row per canonical ICTV species: merged taxids, legacy synonyms, risk profile, segment and host counts |
| `ortho_isolate_table.parquet` | 9,904 × 52 | Reconstructed isolates with S/M/L representatives, triplet status, concatenated protein, divergence diagnostics |
| `ortho_host_table.parquet` | 253 × 13 | One row per host taxon with risk prior and virus species carried |
| `ortho_risk_table.parquet` | 9,904 × 31 | Pathogenicity class, CFR band, citation, and an auditable additive `surveillance_priority_score` |
| `ortho_segment_divergence.parquet` | 9,904 × 17 | Per-segment nearest neighbours and rank separations — **diagnostics, not reassortment calls** |
| `ortho_ml_feature_matrix.parquet` | 7,529 × 228 | Raw features + labels, with `group_id` and `year` for leakage-free CV |
| `ortho_ml_segments.parquet` | 15,781 × 19 | Segment-level table for per-segment models |
| `ortho_suppressed.parquet` | 1,021 × 16 | Non-representative accessions with the reason |
| `ortho_qc_report.parquet` | 15,991 × 11 | Per-accession QC including failed transforms with traceback |
| `ortho_feature_scaling.json` | — | Per-feature mean/std, to be fitted **inside** your CV fold |
| `ortho_summary.json` | — | Provenance, integrity results, counts, methods and stated limitations |

### Risk score

`surveillance_priority_score` is a transparent sum, with every term emitted as its own column so
it can be audited or re-weighted:

| Term | Weight |
|---|---|
| `priority_cfr_term` | 4.0 / 2.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.0 by CFR band |
| `priority_human_spillover_term` | 2.0 if human-derived |
| `priority_taxonomic_incongruence_term` | 1.5 |
| `priority_host_jump_term` | 1.0 |
| `priority_triplet_term` | 1.0 if coding-complete triplet |
| `priority_nss_term` | 0.5 if an NSs ORF is annotated |

This is a triage aid for surveillance, not a validated epidemiological risk model. No term derives
from the k-mer divergence diagnostics — weighting a withdrawn classifier would have propagated an
artefact of sample size into a ranking meant to guide surveillance.

### Using the ML tables

Features are emitted **raw**. Fit scaling inside your cross-validation fold using
`ortho_feature_scaling.json`; the statistics there were computed on the full table and must not be
applied before splitting. Feature selection is unsupervised (top-variance k-mers).

**Split by `group_id` (species) or by `year`.** A random split badly overstates accuracy on this
data, because segments from the same outbreak are near-identical.

---

## Known limitations

- **No reassortment calls.** See above. Requires MAFFT + IQ-TREE.
- **k-mer distances are not PED.** The ICTV 0.1 cutoff needs aligned sequences and ML inference.
- **222 coding-complete triplets** is a ceiling set by the data (1,339 COMPLETE records total),
  not by the pipeline. 1,777 groups have all three segments present at some completeness.
- **2,386 records are `unclassified Orthohantavirus` or genus-only** and carry no species-level
  risk label. They are retained, not discarded.
- **CFR bands are literature ranges, not computed from this data.** Sources conflict; both values
  are recorded where they do.
- **1,719 records have no host** and 3,703 have no collection date.
- Grouping tiers 4 and 5 rarely fire, because `strain` is only populated from BioSample.
- Only the first BioSample accession in a record is resolved.

## Citations

- ICTV *Hantaviridae* / *Orthohantavirus* — species demarcation, segment sizes:
  <https://ictv.global/report/chapter/hantaviridae/hantaviridae/mammantavirinae/orthohantavirus>
- Zoonotic Hantaviridae with global public health significance — pathogenicity, CFR, reservoirs:
  <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10459939/>
- Reassortment events in the evolution of hantaviruses — frequencies, segment constraints:
  <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6153690/>
- ECDC factsheet on orthohantavirus infections:
  <https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/infectious-disease-topics/hantavirus-infection/factsheet-orthohantavirus-infections>
- NCBI Datasets virus data report schema:
  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/docs/v2/reference-docs/data-reports/virus/>

content.text:
## Aims

Build a reproducible pipeline that turns a raw NCBI Datasets **Orthohantavirus** package into analysis-ready tables: accession → isolate → species → host hierarchy, pathogenicity/risk labels, per-segment divergence diagnostics, and ML-ready feature matrices for host-association and risk-classification modeling — all traceable back to NCBI's own fields rather than invented heuristics.

## What's known / established

- **Taxonomy**: `virus.taxId` is unusable directly (553 values, mixes strain-level and legacy/current taxid pairs). The lineage node directly below genus *Orthohantavirus* is the real ICTV species — canonicalizing on it collapses 553 → 39 species.
- **Isolate grouping**: BioSample is present on <1% of records, so grouping runs on a 5-tier fallback cascade keyed mainly on `isolate.name` (96.9% coverage). Yields 1,795 S/M/L-complete groups, 223 coding-complete triplets (capped by NCBI completeness, not the pipeline).
- **Segment/completeness**: NCBI's `completeness` field is authoritative; segment identity resolved via a 5-tier evidence cascade (explicit field → annotation vote → defline → length heuristic → unresolved), leaving only 210 truly unresolved.
- **Host roles**: derived from `host.lineage` rank (not string matching); 33 documented host-jump records (pathogenic species found outside their reservoir order).
- **Pathogenicity/CFR**: curated per-species from literature, with conflicting CFR estimates kept as ranges, not collapsed to a point value. A self-check audit caught and fixed 6 of 38 curated reservoir entries that disagreed with observed data.
- **Reassortment classifier was built, tested, and deliberately withdrawn** — it inverted the literature ranking (flagged ANDV at 72% vs. PUUV at 7.7%, opposite of reported frequencies) because cosine k-mer distance measures within-species diversity/sample size, not tree topology.

## What's done

The pipeline runs end-to-end and is currently producing output: integrity-verified against NCBI's md5sums, 16,022 accessions → 39 species → 9,865 isolates, all 10 output tables (accession, species, isolate, host, risk, divergence, ML feature matrix, ML segments, suppressed, QC) plus `ortho_summary.json` provenance. Deterministic, no absolute paths, ~16s runtime.

## What should be studied more

- **210 unresolved segments** and **~2,386 unclassified/genus-only records** — no species-level risk label currently possible for these.
- **1,719 records missing host, 3,703 missing collection date** — limits temporal/spatial epidemiology.
- **Grouping tiers 4–5 almost never fire** (strain field only populated from BioSample) — isolate reconstruction could improve if strain parsing were extracted from free-text fields instead.
- **Real reassortment detection** — currently only emits diagnostics (`sl_rank_separation`, `m_rank_offset`), explicitly marked `requires_phylogenetic_confirmation`, not calls.
- **True PED / ICTV species demarcation** (cutoff 0.1, WAG model) — current k-mer clustering is an alignment-free proxy only, named `kmer_*` specifically to avoid the false claim of being `ped_*`.
- **`surveillance_priority_score` validation** — it's stated explicitly as a transparent triage heuristic, not a validated epidemiological model; would need outcome data to validate.

## Is MAFFT + IQ-TREE necessary?

**Not necessary for the pipeline as scoped** — and deliberately excluded (README: "No alignment or phylogenetics dependencies"). Everything currently produced (taxonomy, grouping, completeness, host roles, pathogenicity labels, risk score) comes from NCBI's own structured metadata, not from sequence alignment, so adding those dependencies wouldn't improve any of it and would turn a 16-second serial run into a much heavier alignment/tree-building job.

**Necessary only if you want to go beyond what's currently claimed**, specifically:
1. **Actual reassortment calls** — detecting reassortment requires testing topological incongruence between independently-built S, M, and L trees. That's a tree-topology question, and k-mer/cosine distance cannot answer it (proven by the failed classifier above) — only real per-segment alignments (MAFFT) and ML phylogenies (IQ-TREE) capture topology.
2. **True PED values for ICTV species demarcation** — the 0.1 WAG-model cutoff is defined on aligned, ML-inferred pairwise distances, not amino-acid composition distance. Any claim about whether two isolates cross that species boundary needs alignment + ML inference to be defensible.
3. **Any publishable phylogenetic claim** about a specific isolate/reassortant — the pipeline's own outputs are explicit that they are diagnostics, not confirmations, precisely so nobody downstream mistakes a k-mer proxy for a phylogenetic result.

So: leave the pipeline as-is for data preparation and ML feature generation; bring in MAFFT + IQ-TREE only as a separate, targeted follow-up step on the subset of isolates flagged `requires_phylogenetic_confirmation`, if/when you need a real reassortment or species-boundary answer.

17	this script invents:

20	- content level: ``nucleotide.sequenceHash`` (CRC32, emitted per record by NCBI) is
21	                 used for sequence identity and de-duplication. It is independent of
22	                 line endings and platform, so it behaves identically on Linux and

357	    better source. This audit runs on every invocation so the same class of curation
358	    error cannot silently return when SPECIES_RISK is next edited.
359	    """
360	    observed: DefaultDict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
361	    hosts: DefaultDict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
362	    for record in accessions:

364	            observed[record.species_name][record.host_order] += 1
365	            hosts[record.species_name][record.host_name] += 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Orthohantavirus NCBI Datasets production pipeline.

Ingests an NCBI Datasets virus package for Orthohantavirus (taxon 1980442) and produces:
- accession-level records
- canonical species records (ICTV binomial, resolved from virus.lineage)
- isolate-level records reconstructed from S/M/L segments
- host-level records
- pathogenicity / surveillance-risk labels
- reassortment candidate calls
- ML-ready feature tables
- QC, suppression and provenance tables

Reproducibility model
---------------------
Integrity is established against NCBI's own published checksums, not against digests
this script invents:

- file level   : ``md5sum.txt`` shipped inside the package is parsed and verified.
- content level: ``nucleotide.sequenceHash`` (CRC32, emitted per record by NCBI) is
                 used for sequence identity and de-duplication. It is independent of
                 line endings and platform, so it behaves identically on Linux and
                 Windows even when a checkout has mangled the files.

``hashlib`` is still used, but only to hash *our own* outputs and configuration --
never to re-derive something NCBI already published.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import re
import sys
import traceback
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, DefaultDict, Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

VERSION = "2.0.0"

ORTHOHANTAVIRUS_TAXID = 1980442

DATA_REPORT = "data_report.jsonl"
ANNOTATION_REPORT = "annotation_report.jsonl"
BIOSAMPLE_REPORT = "biosample_report.jsonl"
GENOMIC_FASTA = "genomic.fna"
PROTEIN_FASTA = "protein.faa"
MD5SUM_FILE = "md5sum.txt"

YEAR_RE = re.compile(r"(19|20)\d{2}")
# Hot-path patterns. clean_text alone runs ~930k times per invocation, so these are
# compiled once here rather than re-resolved from re's cache on every call.
WHITESPACE_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")
NON_ALNUM_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")
HEX_HASH_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9A-F]{1,8}")
MD5_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{32}")
SEGMENT_STRIP_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9;\s()/-]+")
SEGMENT_PUNCT_RE = re.compile(r"[;()/_-]+")
ATTR_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")

# ICTV Hantaviridae segment sizes: S 1.2-2.1 kb, M 3.4-3.8 kb, L 6.5-6.6 kb.
# https://ictv.global/report/chapter/hantaviridae/hantaviridae/mammantavirinae/orthohantavirus
#
# S and M are used as ICTV states them. L is widened to 6300-6800 rather than 6500-6600:
# submitted L segments cluster just outside the ICTV figure at both ends, and tightening to
# the literal bounds would drop a 6,462 nt record -- unambiguously an L at that length --
# back to 'unresolved'. It changes no length_anomaly flag either way.
SEGMENT_LENGTH_RANGE = {"S": (1200, 2100), "M": (3400, 3800), "L": (6300, 6800)}
# Minimum length at which a segment can plausibly be coding-complete. Slightly below the
# ICTV lower bound because several validated coding-complete records are trimmed to the ORF.
COMPLETE_LENGTH_MIN = {"S": 1100, "M": 3200, "L": 6000}
# Beyond these a record is almost certainly a multi-segment concatenation or a mis-label.
SEGMENT_LENGTH_ABSURD_MAX = {"S": 3000, "M": 5000, "L": 8000}
# How far below the ICTV lower bound a COMPLETE record may fall before it is flagged.
COMPLETE_LENGTH_TOLERANCE = 0.85

KMER_K = 3

# Ranks pulled out of virus.lineage, ordered from broad to narrow. This is the
# "until there is no bigger group" hierarchy -- it is already present in every record.
LINEAGE_RANKS = [
    ("realm", "Riboviria"),
    ("kingdom", "Orthornavirae"),
    ("phylum", "Negarnaviricota"),
    ("subphylum", "Polyploviricotina"),
    ("class", "Bunyaviricetes"),
    ("order", "Elliovirales"),
    ("family", "Hantaviridae"),
    ("subfamily", "Mammantavirinae"),
    ("genus", "Orthohantavirus"),
]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Segment vocabulary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Values actually observed in the ``segment`` field of this package, beyond plain S/M/L:
# 'Partial L', 'S segment', 'M-segment', 'M; medium', 'small (S)', 'medium (M)',
# 'G1', 'G2', 'ANONYMOUS', 's', 'N', 'Small', 'Medium', 'Large', 'middle'.
SEGMENT_FIELD_RULES: List[Tuple[re.Pattern, str]] = [
    (re.compile(r"\b(l|large)\b"), "L"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(m|medium|middle)\b"), "M"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(s|small)\b"), "S"),
    # G1/Gn and G2/Gc are both encoded on the M segment.
    (re.compile(r"\bg[12]\b|\bg[nc]\b"), "M"),
    # 'N' means nucleocapsid, which is the S segment product.
    (re.compile(r"^n$"), "S"),
]

# Derived from the 122 distinct CDS product names in annotation_report.jsonl.
#
# Two related but deliberately different questions are asked of a product name:
#   - which SEGMENT does it imply?  (loose: any nonstructural mention implies S)
#   - which PROTEIN ROLE is it?     (strict: only a true NSs product counts as NSs)
# The shared fragments are defined once here so the two rule tables cannot drift, while
# the intentional differences stay visible as explicit additions.
_RDRP = r"polymerase|\brdrp\b|\bl protein\b|^l$"
_GPC = r"glyco|\bgpc\b|\bg1\b|\bg2\b|\bgn\b|\bgc\b|envelope|polyprotein"
_N = r"nucleocapsid|nucleoprotein|\bn protein\b"
_NSS_STRICT = r"\bnss\b|small non-?structural|non-?structural protein s"

# Order matters: polymerase is checked before glycoprotein because a few deflines
# mention both.
PRODUCT_SEGMENT_RULES: List[Tuple[re.Pattern, str]] = [
    (re.compile(_RDRP + r"|\blarge protein\b"), "L"),
    (re.compile(_GPC + r"|m segment"), "M"),
    # Looser than the NSs role rule on purpose: a bare "nonstructural protein" pins the
    # record to S without asserting it is the NSs product.
    (re.compile(_N + r"|\bnss?\b|nonstructural|non-structural"), "S"),
]

# Which protein a product name represents, used for per-segment protein selection.
PRODUCT_ROLE_RULES: List[Tuple[re.Pattern, str]] = [
    (re.compile(_NSS_STRICT), "NSs"),
    (re.compile(_RDRP), "RdRp"),
    (re.compile(_GPC), "GPC"),
    (re.compile(_N), "N"),
]

SEGMENT_PRIMARY_PRODUCT = {"S": "N", "M": "GPC", "L": "RdRp"}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pathogenicity reference table
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every entry carries its source. Species absent from this table are labelled "unknown"
# and are NEVER silently treated as non-pathogenic.
#
# CFR figures genuinely conflict between sources (HTNV is reported both as ~1% and as
# 5-15%), so the reported range is stored verbatim alongside an ordinal band used for
# modelling. Do not collapse these to a point estimate.

CIT_ZOONOTIC = "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10459939/"
CIT_ECDC = "https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/infectious-disease-topics/hantavirus-infection/factsheet-orthohantavirus-infections"
CIT_REASSORT = "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6153690/"
CIT_ICTV = "https://ictv.global/report/chapter/hantaviridae/hantaviridae/mammantavirinae/orthohantavirus"

# cfr_band ordinal: 0 = no human disease known, 1 = <1%, 2 = 1-15%, 3 = >30%
CFR_BAND_LABEL = {0: "none_known", 1: "low_lt_1pct", 2: "moderate_1_15pct", 3: "high_gt_30pct", -1: "unknown"}

SPECIES_RISK: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {
    "Orthohantavirus hantanense": {
        "abbrev": "HTNV", "syndrome": "HFRS", "cfr_band": 2,
        "cfr_reported": "~1% (PMC10459939); 5-15% (ECDC/other reviews)",
        "reservoir": "Apodemus agrarius", "region": "East Asia", "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus dobravaense": {
        "abbrev": "DOBV", "syndrome": "HFRS", "cfr_band": 2,
        "cfr_reported": "0-15% depending on genotype (Dobrava severe, Kurkino/Saaremaa mild)",
        "reservoir": "Apodemus spp.", "region": "Europe", "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus seoulense": {
        "abbrev": "SEOV", "syndrome": "HFRS", "cfr_band": 1,
        "cfr_reported": "<1%", "reservoir": "Rattus norvegicus", "region": "Worldwide",
        "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus puumalaense": {
        "abbrev": "PUUV", "syndrome": "HFRS/NE", "cfr_band": 1,
        "cfr_reported": "0.1-0.4%", "reservoir": "Myodes glareolus", "region": "Europe",
        "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus andesense": {
        "abbrev": "ANDV", "syndrome": "HCPS", "cfr_band": 3,
        "cfr_reported": "~35-40%; only orthohantavirus with documented person-to-person spread",
        "reservoir": "Oligoryzomys longicaudatus", "region": "Argentina, Chile",
        "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus sinnombreense": {
        "abbrev": "SNV", "syndrome": "HCPS", "cfr_band": 3,
        "cfr_reported": "30-50%", "reservoir": "Peromyscus maniculatus",
        "region": "USA, Canada, Mexico", "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus chocloense": {
        "abbrev": "CHOV", "syndrome": "HCPS", "cfr_band": 2,
        "cfr_reported": "12-15%", "reservoir": "Oligoryzomys fulvescens", "region": "Panama",
        "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus negraense": {
        "abbrev": "LANV", "syndrome": "HCPS", "cfr_band": 2,
        "cfr_reported": "12-15%", "reservoir": "Calomys spp.", "region": "South America",
        "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus mamorense": {
        "abbrev": "RIOMV", "syndrome": "HCPS", "cfr_band": -1,
        "cfr_reported": "human cases reported; CFR not well established",
        "reservoir": "Oligoryzomys microtis", "region": "South America", "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus bayoui": {
        "abbrev": "BAYV", "syndrome": "HCPS", "cfr_band": -1,
        "cfr_reported": "human cases reported; CFR not well established",
        "reservoir": "Oryzomys palustris", "region": "USA", "citation": CIT_ZOONOTIC},
    "Orthohantavirus montanoense": {

# Taxonomic order of each reservoir genus named in SPECIES_RISK. Used to detect records
# where a virus was found outside its expected reservoir order -- e.g. SEOV in Chinese
# shrews and bats, or ANDV-clade sequences in Brazilian bats. Both are real, documented
# detections in this dataset, and a pathogenic rodent-borne virus recovered from a
# non-rodent host is a host-jump signal worth surfacing rather than an error.
RESERVOIR_GENUS_ORDER = {
    # Rodentia
    "Apodemus": "Rodentia", "Rattus": "Rodentia", "Myodes": "Rodentia",
    "Oligoryzomys": "Rodentia", "Peromyscus": "Rodentia", "Calomys": "Rodentia",
    "Oryzomys": "Rodentia", "Microtus": "Rodentia", "Bandicota": "Rodentia",

    "Reithrodontomys": "Rodentia", "Eothenomys": "Rodentia", "Mus": "Rodentia",
    "Stenocephalemys": "Rodentia", "Alexandromys": "Rodentia",
    # Eulipotyphla (shrews and moles)
    "Crocidura": "Eulipotyphla", "Anourosorex": "Eulipotyphla", "Talpa": "Eulipotyphla",
    "Urotrichus": "Eulipotyphla", "Scalopus": "Eulipotyphla", "Sorex": "Eulipotyphla",

def audit_reservoir_curation(accessions: Sequence["AccessionRecord"]) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """Check every curated reservoir against the modal observed host order in the data.

    SPECIES_RISK reservoirs were curated by hand, and six of the original 38 entries
    disagreed with the package's own host annotations at the taxonomic-order level
    (asikkalaense, fugongense, lankaense, luxiense, sagercreekense, tigrayense). Those
    were corrected against the data, which comes from the submitting studies and is the
    better source. This audit runs on every invocation so the same class of curation
    error cannot silently return when SPECIES_RISK is next edited.
    """
    observed: DefaultDict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
    hosts: DefaultDict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
    for record in accessions:
        if record.host_order and record.host_order != "Primates":
            observed[record.species_name][record.host_order] += 1
            hosts[record.species_name][record.host_name] += 1

    findings: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
    for species, entry in SPECIES_RISK.items():
        counts = observed.get(species)
        if not counts:
            continue
        curated = RESERVOIR_GENUS_ORDER.get(entry["reservoir"].split()[0], "")
        modal = mode(counts)
        if not curated:
            findings.append({"species": species, "issue": "reservoir genus not in RESERVOIR_GENUS_ORDER",
                             "curated_reservoir": entry["reservoir"], "modal_observed_host": ""})
        elif curated != modal:
            findings.append({
                "species": species, "issue": "curated reservoir order disagrees with data",
                "curated_reservoir": f"{entry['reservoir']} ({curated})",
                "modal_observed_host": f"{mode(hosts[species])} ({modal})"})
    return findings

def configure_logging(log_file: Path, verbose: bool = False) -> None:
    log_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=level,
        format="%(asctime)s | %(levelname)s | %(message)s",
        # mode="w": one run, one log. Appending made this a 428-line accretion of every run
        # ever done in the checkout, and since it is a tracked file it carried absolute paths
        # (and so usernames) from more than one developer's machine into git.
        handlers=[logging.FileHandler(log_file, mode="w", encoding="utf-8"),
                  logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)],
    )


def clean_text(value: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        text = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
    else:
        text = str(value).strip()
    if not text:
        return None
    if text.lower() in {"none", "null", "nan", "na", "n/a", "unknown", "missing",
                        "not collected", "not provided", "not applicable", "restricted access"}:
        return None
    return WHITESPACE_RE.sub(" ", text).strip()


def first_nonempty(*values: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    for value in values:
        if isinstance(value, list):
            for item in value:
                found = clean_text(item)
                if found:
                    return found
        else:
            found = clean_text(value)
            if found:
                return found
    return None


def uniq(values: Iterable[Any]) -> List[Any]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for value in values:
        key = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) if isinstance(value, (dict, list, tuple, set)) else str(value)
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            out.append(value)
    return out


def mode(counter: Counter, default: str = "") -> str:
    """Most frequent key, or `default` when the counter is empty."""
    return counter.most_common(1)[0][0] if counter else default


def accession_base(accession: str) -> str:
    return accession.split(".")[0] if accession else ""


def indexed_record_count(index: Dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    """Number of distinct records in an index that files each one under several keys.

    build_annotation_index and parse_fasta both key a record on its versioned accession
    and on its base, so len(index) reports roughly twice the number of records read.
    """
    return len({id(value) for value in index.values()})


def iter_jsonl(path: Path) -> Iterator[Dict[str, Any]]:
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line_no, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
                raise ValueError(f"JSON decode error in {path.name} line {line_no}: {exc}") from exc
            if isinstance(obj, dict):
                yield obj

929	        if name not in seen:
930	            results.append(ChecksumResult(
931	                name, want, "", False, "missing",

937	def report_checksums(results: Sequence[ChecksumResult], allow_mismatch: bool) -> None:
938	    failures = [r for r in results if not r.verified]
939	    for result in results:
940	        if result.verified and result.matched_form == "raw":
941	            logging.debug("checksum ok: %s", result.file_name)
942	    listed = [r for r in results if r.matched_form != "unlisted"]
943	    unlisted = len(results) - len(listed)
944	    if not failures:
945	        # Report against the number of files md5sum.txt actually covers. Counting only the
946	        # files that passed on both sides of the ratio made this a tautological 'N/N' that
947	        # stayed silent about files shipped without a published checksum.
948	        logging.info("Integrity: %s/%s files verified against NCBI md5sum.txt%s",
949	                     sum(1 for r in listed if r.verified), len(listed),
950	                     f"; {unlisted} shipped file(s) not listed and not checked" if unlisted else "")
951	        return
952	
953	    for result in failures:
954	        logging.error("CHECKSUM MISMATCH %s", result.file_name)
955	        logging.error("    expected (NCBI): %s", result.expected_md5)
956	        logging.error("    observed (disk): %s", result.observed_md5)
957	        logging.error("    diagnosis      : %s", result.diagnosis)
958	
959	    if not allow_mismatch:
960	        raise SystemExit(
961	            f"\nAborting: {len(failures)} input file(s) do not match NCBI's published checksums.\n"
962	            "Results computed from these bytes would not be reproducible on another platform.\n"
963	            "Re-run with --allow-checksum-mismatch to proceed anyway (the mismatch is recorded "
964	            "in ortho_summary.json)."
965	        )
966	    logging.warning("Continuing despite %s checksum failure(s) because --allow-checksum-mismatch was set.",
967	                    len(failures))

974	    comparison or grouping -- otherwise '5F2C0FB' and '05F2C0FB' look like different

991	def resolve_species(record: Dict[str, Any]) -> SpeciesAssignment:
992	    """Resolve a record to its canonical ICTV species.
993	
994	    The organism-level ``virus.taxId`` is unusable as a species key: in this package it
995	    takes 553 distinct values, mixing strain-level taxa ('Hantaan virus Lee', 'Four
996	    Corners hantavirus') with legacy/current taxid pairs for the same species
997	    ('Puumala orthohantavirus' 1980486 vs 'Orthohantavirus puumalaense' 3052493).
998	
999	    The node immediately below genus Orthohantavirus in ``virus.lineage`` *is* the ICTV
1000	    species, and canonicalising on its binomial name merges the legacy/current pairs.
1001	    That collapses 553 organism values to 38 species plus 'unclassified Orthohantavirus'.
1002	    """
1003	    virus = record.get("virus") or {}
1004	    observed_name = clean_text(virus.get("organismName")) or ""
1005	    observed_taxid = str(virus.get("taxId") or "")
1006	    lineage = virus.get("lineage") or []
1007	
1008	    ranks: Dict[str, str] = {}
1009	    known_ranks = {name: rank for rank, name in LINEAGE_RANKS}
1010	    genus_index = -1
1011	    for index, node in enumerate(lineage):
1012	        if not isinstance(node, dict):
1013	            continue
1014	        name = clean_text(node.get("name")) or ""
1015	        if name in known_ranks:
1016	            ranks[known_ranks[name]] = name
1017	        if node.get("taxId") == ORTHOHANTAVIRUS_TAXID:
1018	            genus_index = index
1019	
1020	    if genus_index < 0:
1021	        return SpeciesAssignment(observed_name or "unassigned", observed_taxid, observed_taxid,
1022	                                 observed_name, "outside_genus", ranks)
1023	
1024	    if genus_index + 1 >= len(lineage):
1025	        return SpeciesAssignment("Orthohantavirus (genus-level only)", str(ORTHOHANTAVIRUS_TAXID),
1026	                                 observed_taxid, observed_name, "genus_only", ranks)
1027	
1028	    species_node = lineage[genus_index + 1]
1029	    species_name = clean_text(species_node.get("name")) or ""
1030	    species_taxid = str(species_node.get("taxId") or "")
1031	
1032	    status = "classified"
1033	    if species_name.lower().startswith("unclassified"):
1034	        status = "unclassified"
1035	
1036	    ranks["species"] = species_name
1037	    return SpeciesAssignment(species_name, species_taxid, observed_taxid, observed_name, status, ranks)

1084	def normalize_segment_field(value: Any) -> str:
1085	    """Normalize NCBI's free-text ``segment`` field to S / M / L.
1086	
1087	    Values observed in this package beyond plain S/M/L include 'Partial L', 'S segment',
1088	    'M-segment', 'M; medium', 'small (S)', 'medium (M)', 'G1', 'G2', 'ANONYMOUS', 's'
1089	    and 'N'. The previous exact-match check ({'S','M','L','SMALL','MEDIUM','LARGE'})
1090	    silently dropped all of these into the length heuristic.
1091	    """
1092	    text = clean_text(value)
1093	    if not text:
1094	        return ""
1095	    low = SEGMENT_STRIP_RE.sub(" ", text.lower())
1096	    low = SEGMENT_PUNCT_RE.sub(" ", low)
1097	    low = WHITESPACE_RE.sub(" ", low).strip()
1098	    if not low or low in {"anonymous", "unknown", "unnamed"}:
1099	        return ""
1100	    for pattern, segment in SEGMENT_FIELD_RULES:
1101	        if pattern.search(low):
1102	            return segment
1103	    return ""

1106	def segment_from_products(products: Sequence[str]) -> str:
1107	    """Infer segment from annotated CDS product names, by majority vote."""
1108	    votes: Counter = Counter()
1109	    for product in products:
1110	        low = (product or "").lower()
1111	        for pattern, segment in PRODUCT_SEGMENT_RULES:
1112	            if pattern.search(low):
1113	                votes[segment] += 1
1114	                break
1115	    if not votes:
1116	        return ""
1117	    top = votes.most_common()
1118	    if len(top) > 1 and top[0][1] == top[1][1]:
1119	        return ""
1120	    return top[0][0]

1139	def choose_segment(
1140	    raw_segment: Any,
1141	    products: Sequence[str],
1142	    defline: str,
1143	    nt_len: int,
1144	) -> Tuple[str, str, float, List[str]]:
1145	    """Resolve segment with an explicit evidence hierarchy and a confidence score."""
1146	    warnings: List[str] = []
1147	
1148	    explicit = normalize_segment_field(raw_segment)
1149	    if explicit:
1150	        return explicit, "explicit", 1.0, warnings
1151	
1152	    from_products = segment_from_products(products)
1153	    if from_products:
1154	        return from_products, "annotation", 0.90, warnings

1174	def determine_completeness(record: Dict[str, Any], segment: str, nt_len: int) -> Tuple[str, str, bool]:
1175	    """Return (completeness, source, is_coding_complete).
1176	
1177	    NCBI's structured ``completeness`` is present on 100% of records in this package
1178	    (PARTIAL 14,652 / COMPLETE 1,339) and is authoritative. The previous implementation
1179	    carried an elaborate cascade of definition-line text matching, ambiguous-base counting
1180	    and terminal-panhandle motif checks that never executed. Length is used only to
1181	    qualify a COMPLETE call for coding-completeness, never to override NCBI.
1182	    """
1183	    raw = clean_text(record.get("completeness")) or ""
1184	    low = raw.lower()
1185	    if low == "complete":
1186	        if not segment:
1187	            return "complete", "ncbi", False
1188	        coding_complete = nt_len >= COMPLETE_LENGTH_MIN.get(segment, 10 ** 9)
1189	        return "complete", "ncbi", coding_complete
1190	    if low == "partial":
1191	        return "partial", "ncbi", False
1192	    if low:
1193	        return low, "ncbi", False
1194	    return "unknown", "absent", False

1197	def length_anomaly(segment: str, nt_len: int, completeness: str) -> str:
1198	    """Flag lengths that contradict the ICTV segment size ranges.
1199	
1200	    Only complete records are checked against the lower bound: a partial sequence is
1201	    *expected* to be short, and the previous rule ('M' and not 1500 <= n <= 5000) fired
1202	    on 5,856 records, almost all of them legitimately partial.
1203	    """
1204	    if not segment or not nt_len:
1205	        return ""
1206	    absurd_max = SEGMENT_LENGTH_ABSURD_MAX.get(segment)
1207	    if absurd_max and nt_len > absurd_max:
1208	        return "length_exceeds_segment_maximum"
1209	    if completeness == "complete":
1210	        lo, _hi = SEGMENT_LENGTH_RANGE[segment]
1211	        if nt_len < lo * COMPLETE_LENGTH_TOLERANCE:
1212	            return "complete_but_shorter_than_ictv_range"
1213	    return ""
